stories.title: Direct attacks on ships in Hormuz
stories.what: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz have continued into November, including a VLCC whose engine room was struck in Omani waters. Today UKMTO is reported to have logged a further tanker strike.
stories.why_it_matters: Strikes on hulls raise war-risk premiums and crew-safety objections for Arabian Gulf liftings, shrinking the pool of willing owners and supporting crude and product tanker earnings.
stories.latest: A Hormuz tanker strike reported by UKMTO, and South Korea said it wants to deploy naval assets closer to the strait.
sources: US-sanctioned ships dropped from Iran's PGSA blacklist
South Korea Plans to Deploy Naval Assets Closer to Hormuz

stories.title: Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab transits and Gulf congestion
stories.what: Strait of Hormuz traffic rose in October to its highest monthly level since July, supported by dry bulk and LNG movements even as VLCC traffic declined. Red Sea traffic also rose and Arabian Gulf waiting remains elevated.
stories.why_it_matters: Transit counts and waiting times show whether ships route through or around high-risk waters, changing voyage lengths, tonne-mile demand and effective fleet supply.

stories.title: Sanctions and evasion in the shadow fleet
stories.what: The US sanctioned a network running fraudulent ship registries and false-flag services for Iranian shadow fleet vessels, and today expanded sanctions to five ships and two people tied to Cuba's oil shipping network. Separately, seven sanctioned Russian tankers were found manipulating AIS to disguise Novorossiysk voyages.
stories.why_it_matters: Registry fraud and AIS spoofing force charterers, insurers and class societies to re-verify documentation and positions, and can push sanctioned tonnage out of mainstream trades, tightening compliant tanker supply.
stories.latest: US State Department sanctioned five ships and two people over Cuban oil shipping; seven sanctioned tankers reported spoofing AIS near the Bosphorus; US-sanctioned LPG carriers removed from Iran's PGSA non-compliance list.
sources: U.S. State Department Expands Sanctions on Cuban Shipping
Seven Shadow Fleet Tankers Spoof AIS to Hide Novorossiysk Voyages
US-sanctioned ships dropped from Iran's PGSA blacklist

stories.title: Drone attacks on shipping in the western Black Sea
stories.what: A Greek container ship sank after being hit by naval drones off Bulgaria, the latest in a series of strikes in the western Black Sea.
stories.why_it_matters: Attacks on ships and port infrastructure threaten grain and dry bulk loadings from the region and add insurance and routing costs for any vessel calling there.

stories.title: Russian diesel flows and export restrictions
stories.what: A reported US-Russia agreement on supplying extra diesel to the US market has met political opposition, while Russia has extended a general ban on most diesel exports until the end of January, with some volumes still allowed to flow.
stories.why_it_matters: Diesel export restrictions and any reopened Atlantic route reshape clean product tanker ton-miles and MR and LR employment patterns.

stories.title: Port labour disruption in the US and Europe
stories.what: A contract standoff involving 250 security workers threatens to freeze operations across Los Angeles and Long Beach terminals after a 4 November deadline extension, while dockworkers struck across Europe and beyond over arms shipments.
stories.why_it_matters: Labour action at container and ferry berths disrupts berthing schedules and cargo flows, and the unresolved US West Coast dispute leaves a large share of US import capacity exposed to stoppage.
